analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation row added to the scheduler configuration table in docs/architecture/inference.md (head line 850). It describes prompt-chunk attention: 128-query blocks, a fused `.causal` path for eligible full-attention chunks, and the `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0` rollback switch. The row cites AttentionV1.swift (`usesFusedCausalPrefill`) and PagedLayerCache.swift (`prefillAttend`). The PR modifies no source, keys, wire protocol, authorization, or cache-storage code, so no controls are weakened by it. The supplied units are a base excerpt (lines 1622-1777) and a head excerpt (lines 1-415). Neither excerpt contains the added table row, which sits at head line 850 and is visible only in the patch. The patch itself is complete. The doc row says the fused path applies on either KV backend. That is a runtime attention-kernel choice and does not affect prefix-cache identity, salt scoping, SSD encryption, TTL, or the HMAC lookup tags covered by T-041. T-041 and SEC-035 are unchanged in kind. Remaining integration question, outside the supplied evidence: whether the actual Swift/MLX kernel change that this documentation row describes preserves attention masking and per-request isolation. That change is not in this batch. Per T-028 and T-041, cross-request leakage through the attention path would require reviewing those source files. A documentation-only change cannot establish that, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
